Symptom Guide

Hernia Symptoms

Recognizing hernia symptoms early can prevent complications. Learn what signs to watch for and when medical attention is needed.

Seek Help Now Get Diagnosed

Symptom Checker

Do you have these symptoms?

Most Common

Visible Bulge

A lump or swelling in the groin, abdomen, or belly button area. Often more visible when standing, coughing, or straining.

Usually appears gradually
Key Symptom

Pain or Discomfort

Aching, burning, or sharp pain at the hernia site. May worsen with physical activity, heavy lifting, or prolonged standing.

Often worsens through the day
Characteristic

Heaviness

Feeling of heaviness or dragging sensation in the groin or abdomen, as if something is weighing you down.

May be worse after activity
Related

Straining

Discomfort when coughing, sneezing, or making bowel movements. Activities that increase abdominal pressure hurt.

Occurs with physical strain
Positive Sign

Reducible

Bulge may push back in or disappear when lying down. The hernia contents can be gently returned to their normal position.

Means less urgent risk
Progressive

Growing Over Time

The hernia gradually increases in size over weeks or months. What was once small is now more noticeable.

Indicates worsening condition

Symptoms by Hernia Type

Different hernias may have unique symptom patterns

Hernia Type Common Location Typical Symptoms Unique Features
Inguinal Groin, inner thigh Bulge, pain, heaviness More common in men; pain may extend to testicles
Femoral Upper thigh, below groin Small bulge, groin pain More common in women; higher complication risk
Umbilical Belly button Visible bulge at navel Often painless; more common in infants and obese adults
Incisional Previous surgical scar Bulge at incision site May have numbness around scar; size varies greatly
Ventral/Epigastric Upper abdomen, midline Small bulge, localized pain Often painless; fatty tissue only; may be multiple
Hiatal Internal (chest area) Heartburn, chest pain, reflux No visible bulge; causes digestive symptoms

When to See Dr. Kumar

Schedule an appointment if you notice these signs

Visible Bulge That Persists

Any lump that doesn't go away or isn't easily pushed back in.

Pain That Worsens

Increasing pain at the site or spreading to other areas.

Size That's Increasing

A growing hernia means it's weakening further.

Nausea or Vomiting

Digestive symptoms combined with a bulge need evaluation.

Can't Pass Gas or Stool

Family History of Hernias

If hernias run in your family, early screening is wise.

Emergency Warning Signs

Go to the emergency room immediately if you experience these

Strangulation

Blood supply to the herniated tissue is cut off. This is a surgical emergency.

Warning Signs:

  • Severe, constant pain
  • Bulge becomes firm and tender
  • Skin changes (redness, darkening)
  • Nausea, vomiting, fever

Incarceration & Obstruction

Warning Signs:

  • Bulge won't go back in
  • Severe abdominal distension
  • Unable to pass gas or stool
  • Cramping, vomiting
